titleEn: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver: A Homeowner's Complete Guide (2026)
titleZh: 温哥华 Poly-B 水管更换完整指南 (2026)
contentEn:
Poly-B (polybutylene) pipes were installed in an estimated 100,000+ Metro Vancouver homes between 1978 and 1996. If your home falls in that age range and uses Poly-B plumbing, you are sitting on a time bomb: the pipes fail unpredictably, often without warning, and standard home insurance increasingly refuses to cover Poly-B-related water damage. This guide tells you exactly what Poly-B replacement costs in Vancouver in 2026, what your options are, and how to protect your home before a catastrophic leak occurs.

What Is Poly-B Pipe and Why Does It Fail?

Polybutylene (Poly-B) is a plastic resin pipe that was marketed as a cheaper, easier-to-install alternative to copper. It was used for hot and cold water distribution lines, and fittings were joined with acetal plastic or copper crimp rings. The problem is not the pipe itself but the fittings: oxidation and chloramine exposure cause the plastic fittings to become brittle, crack, and fail. A fitting that costs $2 to replace can cause $40,000 in water damage if no one is home when it lets go.

How Much Does Poly-B Replacement Cost in Vancouver in 2026?

Based on quotes from licensed Vancouver plumbers in 2025-2026, Poly-B replacement costs range from $4,500 for a basic townhouse repipe to $18,000+ for a large single-family home, depending on the number of fixtures and accessibility.

  • Townhouse / condo: $4,500-$7,000 (simplest layout, easier access)
  • Single-family home, under 2,000 sq ft: $7,000-$11,000
  • Single-family home, 2,000-3,500 sq ft: $11,000-$15,000
  • Large home / heritage home with plaster walls: $15,000-$18,000+

These figures include labour, materials, permit fees (typically $150-$400 per permit), and wall patching. Full repiping takes 4-10 working days depending on home size.

Does Home Insurance Still Cover Poly-B in BC?

Most major insurers in BC now require a Poly-B disclosure form, and many have either excluded Poly-B coverage entirely or charge a significantly higher premium for homes with Poly-B plumbing. Check with your insurer before you buy a home — a home inspector's Poly-B flag can also affect your ability to insure the property at all. Some insurers will provide coverage if you provide a plumber's certificate confirming the Poly-B system has been inspected and is in acceptable condition.

The Vancouver Poly-B Replacement Process

A professional Poly-B replacement in Vancouver follows these steps: (1) a licensed plumber inspects the system and issues a written assessment; (2) a plumbing permit is obtained from the City of Vancouver (or respective municipality); (3) the plumber isolates and drains the existing system; (4) exposed pipes in basements and crawl spaces are removed first, then the plumber works room by room; (5) new PEX or copper lines are run, connecting to each fixture; (6) the system is pressure-tested and inspected; (7) drywall and finishing work closes the walls back up. Reno Stars manages the full coordination, including city permits and post-job patching, so homeowners do not manage multiple contractors.

Is Repiping Worth It? The Math on Poly-B vs. Water Damage

The average insurance claim for a major water damage event in a Vancouver home is $35,000-$70,000, not including temporary housing costs while the home dries out and is repaired. A single catastrophic failure in a two-storey home can affect both floors simultaneously. For $11,000-$15,000, a full repipe eliminates that risk permanently and can also improve water pressure, which many Poly-B homeowners cite as a secondary benefit.

FAQ: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver

How do I know if my home has Poly-B pipes?

Poly-B pipes are typically grey, silver, or black with copper-coloured fittings. They are usually visible in the basement, crawl space, or where pipes enter walls. A home inspector can confirm within an hour. Homes built between 1978 and 1996 in North Vancouver, West Vancouver, Burnaby, Coquitlam, Richmond, and Surrey are the highest-risk areas.

Can I just replace the fittings instead of the whole system?

Partial repairs are a short-term risk reduction only. The pipe itself is also degrading, and a fitting repair addresses one failure point while dozens of others remain. Most plumbers will not warranty a partial repair. Full repiping is the only permanent solution.

What pipe material is used for replacement?

Cross-linked polyethylene (PEX) pipe is the modern standard for residential repiping in Vancouver. It is flexible, freeze-resistant, and carries a 25-year manufacturer warranty. Copper is still used for certain applications but is more expensive and harder to install in tight spaces.

Do I need a permit for Poly-B replacement in Vancouver?

Yes. A plumbing permit is required from your municipality. In the City of Vancouver this is obtained through the Permits and Licences portal. A licensed plumber typically handles the permit application as part of their service. Permit fees range from $150 to $400 depending on the scope of work.

How long does a full Poly-B repipe take?

For a typical Vancouver single-family home: 4-7 working days for a plumber's crew. Finishing and painting adds another 2-3 days. The project can be fully completed within two weeks in most cases.

Poly-B（聚丁烯）水管于1978年至1996年间在温哥华地区约10万户以上的家庭中安装。如果您的房屋在此年代范围内且使用Poly-B水管，您正面临一个隐患：这些水管会不可预测地破裂，往往毫无预兆，且越来越多的房屋保险公司拒绝承保Poly-B相关的水损事故。本指南详细说明2026年温哥华Poly-B更换的实际费用、可行方案，以及如何在灾难性漏水发生前保护您的房屋。

什么是Poly-B水管？为何会故障？

聚丁烯（Poly-B）是一种塑料树脂水管，当年作为铜管的廉价替代品被广泛使用。问题不在管道本身，而在于连接件：氧化和氯胺侵蚀导致塑料连接件变脆、破裂并失效。一个成本仅2加元的连接件一旦失效，可能造成4万加元的水损。

2026年温哥华Poly-B更换费用

根据2025-2026年温哥华持牌水管工的报价，Poly-B更换费用从4,500加元到18,000加元以上不等。

  • 联排别墅/公寓：4,500-7,000加元
  • 2,000平方尺以下独立屋：7,000-11,000加元
  • 2,000-3,500平方尺独立屋：11,000-15,000加元
  • 大型/老房：15,000-18,000加元以上

含人工、材料、许可费（150-400加元）及墙体修补。全屋重铺4-10个工作日。

BC省保险是否仍承保Poly-B？

BC省大多数主要保险公司现在要求填写Poly-B披露表格，许多公司已完全排除Poly-B承保范围。购房前请务必咨询保险公司。部分保险公司在您提供持牌水管工出具的检验合格证书后可提供承保。

温哥华Poly-B更换流程

（1）持牌水管工检查并出具书面评估；（2）向当地市政厅申请水管许可证；（3）隔离并排空现有系统；（4）逐房间拆除并铺设新PEX管道；（5）系统压力测试并接受检验；（6）修补并还原墙体。Reno Stars负责全程协调，屋主无需对接多个承包商。

更换值得吗？

温哥华房屋重大水损的平均保险理赔金额为35,000-70,000加元，还不包括临时安置费用。对于11,000-15,000加元的全屋更换费用，可以永久消除这一风险。

常见问题：温哥华Poly-B水管更换

如何确认我家是否有Poly-B水管？

Poly-B水管通常为灰色、银色或黑色，带铜色连接件，在地下室或爬空间可见。1978-1996年间建于北温、西温、本拿比、高贵林、列治文及素里的房屋风险最高。

能否只更换连接件？

部分维修只是短期风险降低。管道本身也在老化，一处维修只能解决一个故障点，其他数十个故障点依然存在。全屋重铺是唯一永久解决方案。

更换用什么管道材料？

交联聚乙烯（PEX)是温哥华住宅重铺的行业标准。柔韧、抗冻，附带25年厂家保修。

需要申请许可吗？

需要。向当地市政厅申请水管许可证，许可费用150-400加元。持牌水管工通常代为办理申请。

全屋重铺需要多长时间？

典型温哥华独立屋：水暖工施工队需4-7个工作日，补漆另需2-3天。整个项目通常可在两周内竣工。
